keyFindings.text: **`ROUTER.md` and `references/README.md` contribute no format constraint, and their precedence rule is inverted by the template's.** The router delegates format entirely to the template and, on any `global_component` match, loads the whole flat inventory rather than a chosen subset. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/ROUTER.md:23] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/ROUTER.md:33] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/ROUTER.md:135] Its pseudocode loads every discovered markdown file in one pass. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/ROUTER.md:137] So a run takes the template and `worked-examples.md` together, and `worked-examples.md` re-asserts the Expanded gate and points at the exemplar. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/references/worked-examples.md:25] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/references/worked-examples.md:83] The precedence order is also mutually inconsistent: `references/README.md` says nothing overrides `SKILL.md` or the template and "When they conflict, those two win". [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/references/README.md:23] The template says the exemplar wins over the template. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/assets/changelog-template.md:31] Both rules are live in one load. **Unresolved contradiction, recorded not resolved**: the packet has no single top of the precedence chain.

**Each H4 item is allowed up to seven paragraphs, with one or two as the stated norm.** The template slot for an item reads "One or two paragraphs for most items, seven at most". [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/assets/changelog-template.md:101] The length table gives the same pair. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/assets/changelog-template.md:208] `SKILL.md` validation check 9 imports the seven-paragraph ceiling. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/SKILL.md:259] The worked example's own annotation is stricter than either, at one paragraph per item. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/references/worked-examples.md:112] A permitted maximum of seven is a drafting affordance the short entry never uses: a 22-item entry at the permitted maximum runs well past the exemplar itself. This is a supporting push rather than a primary one, since the stated norm is compatible with the short format. [INFERENCE: the norm and the maximum diverge by 3.5x, and a generator holding a large source will trend toward the maximum]

**Expanded has no file-total ceiling, and every ceiling in the length table is calibrated against the 535-line exemplar.** The length table's only file-total row is "Compact file total | 10-25 lines of prose | 40 lines of prose". [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/assets/changelog-template.md:210] The text under the table states the calibration explicitly: "each one sits at or above what the exemplar does, so the exemplar passes every check it teaches". [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/assets/changelog-template.md:212] Validation check 9 enumerates the ceilings that hold and ends at "compact files within 40 prose lines", confirming the expanded total is unconstrained. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/SKILL.md:259] Working the other expanded ceilings together (opening to 5 paragraphs, 12 glance bullets, H4 narrative to 7 paragraphs, no item count) leaves the long form legal by construction. This is the finding that makes finding 1 unrecoverable: even a writer who wanted to be concise has no ceiling to hit once Expanded is selected.

**No worked model exists at the scale the short format occupies, so the packet brackets it from both sides.** Section 2 is a compact entry whose glance list has two bullets and whose Upgrade section is one line. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/references/worked-examples.md:35] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/references/worked-examples.md:68] Section 3 is an Expanded excerpt gated to "10 or more changes, a major bump or a breaking change". [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/references/worked-examples.md:81] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/references/worked-examples.md:83] The stated uses confirm the narrow range: "what the selection rules leave out of a compact entry" and "how an expanded section reads before writing one". [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/references/worked-examples.md:30] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/references/worked-examples.md:31] A writer with a many-change release has no worked model of moderate length, so the only model left is the 535-line exemplar. The one lean example is explicitly a corrective: it is "a leaner rewrite of this packet's published v1.3.1.0 entry". [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/references/worked-examples.md:37]

**Selection opens with an exhaustive-enumeration instruction and validation adds no upper bound on items.** The template's selection step begins "List every change the source records", with the reader-impact filter placed second. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/assets/changelog-template.md:133] The generation step carries the same order of operations. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/SKILL.md:198] Validation requires "at least one topical H2 with H4 items" and an omission check, so a 5-item and a 40-item entry both pass. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/SKILL.md:255] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/SKILL.md:257] A generator that enumerates first and filters under time pressure keeps the enumeration.

**Small fixes have no container: the sole instruction is to compress them into one sentence or drop them, and the instruction lives under a heading that forbids keeping them.** The Drop-by-Default heading owns the item "Small fixes with no visible effect. Fold several into one sentence, or leave them out." [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/assets/changelog-template.md:143] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/assets/changelog-template.md:151] Both permitted outcomes are prose-level; neither creates a place to put a grouped list of small fixes, which is what the short entry uses. No heading rule supplies one either, since the H4 rule only constrains word count. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/assets/changelog-template.md:121] Structurally the packet says these items should shrink to nothing while the target format gives them their own block, so a generator obeying the packet never builds the block.

**The exemplar clause makes a 535-line file authoritative for shape, and the length hedge sits inside the same sentence that grants it precedence.** The template instructs the writer to read the exemplar before writing, then: "Copy its voice and shape, not its length" and "When this template and the exemplar disagree on shape, the exemplar wins and the discrepancy is recorded". [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/assets/changelog-template.md:31] `SKILL.md` converts this into an unfalsifiable test: "Every entry must be able to sit beside the canonical exemplar, `.skilled/changelog/skilled/v4.0.0.0.md`, without looking out of place." [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/SKILL.md:100] The exemplar is also named the thing the template "derives from". [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/assets/changelog-template.md:260] The push is triangulated from two more directions: `worked-examples.md` sends an Expanded writer to the exemplar for "the full expanded shape". [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/references/worked-examples.md:25] and `references/README.md` lists it as "Real entry to model". [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/references/README.md:53] Because no check measures expanded length (finding 3), "shape" is the only operative word and there is nothing to stop shape from absorbing length. [INFERENCE: based on the precedence grant at line 31 combined with the absent expanded total at line 210, which leaves length inside the scope of "shape" that the exemplar wins]

**The format system is a two-party binary, restated at four definition sites, and it has no third tier for a many-change concise entry.** The template calls itself "The two-tier narrative format" in both its `description` and its purpose line. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/assets/changelog-template.md:3] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/assets/changelog-template.md:23] Section 2 is titled "THE TWO TIERS" and defines only "Compact Format (under 10 changes, non-breaking)" and "Expanded Format (10+ changes, major or breaking)". [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/assets/changelog-template.md:35] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/assets/changelog-template.md:39] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/assets/changelog-template.md:72] The binary is re-asserted in the format contract's items 2 and 3, in the generation step, and in validation check 5, which requires "the tier's sections" and therefore admits no entry outside the two tiers. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/SKILL.md:105] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/SKILL.md:106] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/SKILL.md:199] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/SKILL.md:255] The packet `README.md` repeats it twice more. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/README.md:29] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/README.md:64] The short v4.0.1.0 entry, at 10+ changes, is routed to Expanded by rule and is legally neither Compact (it exceeds the 40-prose-line compact total) nor shaped like Expanded (it omits the opening narrative's five-paragraph allowance and folds small fixes). This is the highest-leverage push toward the long format, because it fires before any content decision is made.

**The packet's only remedy for a long entry is prose-level editing, never re-selection to a shorter shape.** The troubleshooting table's row for "Entry runs long or repeats itself" prescribes "Apply the template's section 3" -- the content filter -- and nothing else. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/README.md:101] The workflow's quality step likewise says to "Apply the cut test (template section 3)". [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/SKILL.md:205] Once the format is chosen at the generation step, no later step can undo it: there is no re-selection gate, no body-length check and no escalation on overrun. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/SKILL.md:199] The failure mode is therefore self-reinforcing rather than merely unpunished.

**The push is concentrated in one file and mirrored in four places; `version-bump-rules.md` and `topology-edge-cases.md` are clean, and one of them supplies the corrective pattern.** `version-bump-rules.md` separates effort from bump with the rule "Major means a breaking or architectural change, not high effort". [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/references/version-bump-rules.md:48] That is the exact structural move the format system lacks: a "large is not long" counterpart to "large is not major", in the same file family and the same voice. `topology-edge-cases.md` carries no format rule and routes every format conflict back to the template. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/references/topology-edge-cases.md:64] Ranking the surface by leverage: `assets/changelog-template.md` holds the primary push (findings 1-10 all trace to it), `SKILL.md` mirrors it into the executable contract at §5, §7 and §9 (findings 1, 3, 4, 7, 9, 10, 11, 14), `references/worked-examples.md` supplies the models and the gate restatement (findings 2, 5, 6, 13), the packet `README.md` restates the binary and the remedy (findings 1, 11), and `ROUTER.md` plus `references/README.md` are neutral witnesses that nonetheless load everything at once and disagree on precedence (finding 12). Negative results recorded so Q5 need not search them again.

**The selection guide mandates Expanded for exactly the case the short entry represents.** The table pairs "Major release (10+ changes)" with Expanded and "Breaking change" with Expanded "regardless of count". [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/assets/changelog-template.md:222] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/assets/changelog-template.md:223] The decision tree below it repeats both branches without a conciseness escape. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/assets/changelog-template.md:230] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/assets/changelog-template.md:231] `worked-examples.md` restates the same gate above its one Expanded example. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/references/worked-examples.md:83] The change count is what a generator can measure, so this is the deterministic branch a many-change release takes.

**The spec-folder line is mandated with a `(Level {N})` suffix, and no rule or check governs that suffix.** Both tier templates carry ``> Spec folder: `{path}` (Level {N})``. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/assets/changelog-template.md:55] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/assets/changelog-template.md:79] The format contract's item 4 restates it. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/SKILL.md:107] Validation check 4 tests presence only. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/SKILL.md:254] Meanwhile the same file bans "internal labels such as task or requirement IDs, scenario IDs and packet or phase numbers" while declaring the spec-folder line "the one pointer an entry needs". [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/assets/changelog-template.md:148] A level number sits on the one line the label rule exempts, and the template never says whether `(Level {N})` is required, optional or exemplary. **Unresolved contradiction, recorded not resolved**: the Drop list forbids the internal-label class, the contract mandates one member of it, and nothing tests the shape.

**The success criteria bind correctness to the two tiers and reduce audience fit to an unmeasured phrase.** `SKILL.md` §12 requires that "The entry follows the template's compact or expanded shape and reads in the v4 style: why first, benefit-led headings, only what the reader needs and each fact said once." [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/SKILL.md:342] "Only what the reader needs" is the sole audience test, and none of the ten §9 checks operationalize it; all ten are structural or ceiling checks. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/SKILL.md:249] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/SKILL.md:260] As written, a third format would fail §12 regardless of how well it served the reader.

**Topical-domain guidance caps the count at one to five but re-opens it by reference to the exemplar's size.** The field guideline reads "Most releases need one to five domains. A release the exemplar's size may need more when each one earns its section." [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/assets/changelog-template.md:120] The escape hatch is again sized against the long artifact, and the same file keeps the exemplar in view as the measuring stick elsewhere. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/assets/changelog-template.md:170] Moderate push: the topical-section shape itself transfers to the short format, and only the exemplar-relative escape does not.

**Upgrade Notes are typed by action (Adopt, Repoint, Drop), which cannot express the short entry's section ordering.** The Expanded template's Upgrade Notes body is three fixed lead-ins. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/assets/changelog-template.md:111] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/assets/changelog-template.md:112] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/assets/changelog-template.md:113] The field guideline permits plain bullets only when the release lacks one of the three kinds of work, not when the writer wants a different ordering. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/assets/changelog-template.md:123] The worked example's excerpt uses the action-typed shape and its annotation reinforces it. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/references/worked-examples.md:102] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/references/worked-examples.md:114] Neither `SKILL.md`'s five non-negotiables nor the §9 checks give upgrade notes an ordering rule at all; non-negotiable 4 covers only the inline `**Breaking:**` marker. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/SKILL.md:223] A release ordered by section is therefore off-contract, and the action-typed block is the one shape the packet teaches.

**Contradictory evidence: the two workflow files have drifted, and the unattended path is the stricter one.** Auto carries a WRITING STYLE block of five reader-facing constraints, including "Plain English for a smart person who is not a developer" [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/create/assets/create-changelog-auto.yaml:299], "Lead with why the release matters, never technical stats" [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/create/assets/create-changelog-auto.yaml:300] and "Keep only what the reader would notice or act on" [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/create/assets/create-changelog-auto.yaml:302], plus its own FORMAT SELECTION comment [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/create/assets/create-changelog-auto.yaml:293]. Confirm's corresponding block ends at the tier names and the exemplar lines and contains neither comment [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/create/assets/create-changelog-confirm.yaml:291]. Same source document, two modes, different constraint sets: the autonomous path is told to write plain English for a non-developer, and the interactive path is not. Both sides are cited and the conflict is left unresolved rather than smoothed; direction of resolution is a Q5 decision (probably: hoist the block into the shared template or into both files identically). No operator is present, so this is recorded, not escalated to a halt.
sources: `.skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/references/README.md:47` (names the presentation file as the command-surface asset)

keyFindings.text: **Exemplar and scale clauses push long, and the command surface inherits the template's default instead of counterbalancing it.** `style_reference` names the 535-line v4.0.0.0 entry [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/create/assets/create-changelog-auto.yaml:314], [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/create/assets/create-changelog-confirm.yaml:294], and the section-naming comment authorises scaling to it: "One to five domains for most releases, more for a release the size of the exemplar" [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/create/assets/create-changelog-auto.yaml:322], [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/create/assets/create-changelog-confirm.yaml:302]. The autonomous path further budgets body per item — "H4 items: the detail" [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/create/assets/create-changelog-auto.yaml:584] and "One or two paragraphs, seven at most" [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/create/assets/create-changelog-auto.yaml:573] — with no aggregate cap. Because the YAML defers full rules to template Section 5 [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/create/assets/create-changelog-auto.yaml:541], the command surface adds no counterweight to the template's Expanded default; it localises it three more times.
sources: `.skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/references/README.md:47` (names the presentation file as the command-surface asset)

keyFindings.text: **Format compliance is a hard gate whose verification is satisfied most easily by the long format.** `H3_version_contract` states that "Version calculation and content format must be valid before write" [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/create/assets/create-changelog-auto.yaml:343] and its verification is "All required sections present in generated content" [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/create/assets/create-changelog-auto.yaml:347]. Expanded supplies Why This Release, topical H2 sections, H4 items and Upgrade Notes, so it passes that gate by construction; a concise entry that merges sections risks failing it. The gate as written rewards section count.
sources: `.skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/references/README.md:47` (names the presentation file as the command-surface asset)

keyFindings.text: **Keep/drop wording points short at selection time but never at output size, and the one rule the short entry needs — fold small fixes into a single bullet list — is absent.** The autonomous path selects content by reader impact: "Keep a change only when the reader would notice it, act on it or decide differently because of it", merge same-effect changes, rank by impact, and "Drop test and playbook changes, internal labels, process detail and follow-on housekeeping" [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/create/assets/create-changelog-auto.yaml:533], [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/create/assets/create-changelog-auto.yaml:535]. The omission rules repeat the floor for every format: no Files Changed tables, no test metrics, no schema tables, no internal labels outside the spec-folder line, reverted mid-cycle work compressed to one story sentence, tables only when the numbers are the story [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/create/assets/create-changelog-auto.yaml:577]. The interactive path keeps a compressed version [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/create/assets/create-changelog-confirm.yaml:527]. All of this is per-item elimination; nothing says what to do when the surviving set is still large, and nothing permits folding a group of small fixes into one bullet list. Sub-part 6's answer is split: the keep/drop lists push short, the per-item scope leaves the aggregate body unbounded.
sources: `.skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/references/README.md:47` (names the presentation file as the command-surface asset)

keyFindings.text: **No length, body-size or item-count gate exists anywhere on the command surface; every quantitative cap is per-unit and nothing caps how many units there are.** A grep for `max`, `maximum`, `ceiling`, `cap`, `limit`, `total lines`, `total words` and `prose lines` across both YAMLs returns zero hits. The only numbers are per-unit: summary "1-2 sentences, 3 at most" compact and "1-3 paragraphs, 5 at most" expanded [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/create/assets/create-changelog-auto.yaml:559], H4 headings "10 words at most" and H4 items "7 paragraphs at most" [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/create/assets/create-changelog-auto.yaml:647], and the same limits restated in confirm's content checks [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/create/assets/create-changelog-confirm.yaml:583]. Section count is an output and a report field, never a gate [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/create/assets/create-changelog-auto.yaml:617]. The quality standards set a floor and no ceiling: content quality's minimum is "Summary narrative + at-a-glance + upgrade notes" [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/create/assets/create-changelog-auto.yaml:779] and format compliance's is "All required sections present" [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/create/assets/create-changelog-auto.yaml:773].
sources: `.skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/references/README.md:47` (names the presentation file as the command-surface asset)

keyFindings.text: **No setup field or prompt asks for a change count, so `change_count` is workflow-computed and Expanded is a machine-selected outcome with no operator decision.** The presentation contract's resolution table has six fields — `source_type`, `spec_folder`, `component_hint`, `version_bump`, `execution_mode`, `publish_release` — and none is a change count [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/create/assets/create-changelog-presentation.txt:69], which the startup prompt mirrors as Q0/Q1/Q2/Q3 with no count question [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/create/assets/create-changelog-presentation.txt:99]. The YAML input contract agrees: required `create_agent_verified` and `source_type`, optional `spec_folder`, `component_hint`, `version_bump`, `publish_release` [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/create/assets/create-changelog-auto.yaml:154]. `change_count` appears only inside step 4, where it is derived locally [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/create/assets/create-changelog-auto.yaml:539]. In the autonomous path nothing intervenes between that derivation and the tier, because approvals are disabled outright [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/create/assets/create-changelog-auto.yaml:31]. In the interactive path a step-4 checkpoint exists, but its options are Approve / Review / Modify / Regenerate [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/create/assets/create-changelog-confirm.yaml:570] — there is no "use the shorter format" option, so even the human-in-the-loop path cannot overrule the tier.
sources: `.skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/references/README.md:47` (names the presentation file as the command-surface asset)

keyFindings.text: **The command doc carries no format guidance at all — it is a pure router, so no format rule can be fixed there.** It calls itself "a thin router" that separates "execution routing from user-facing presentation" [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/create/changelog.md:9], states that "The YAML owns workflow behavior; the presentation Markdown owns user-visible wording and layout" [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/create/changelog.md:34], and forbids the router from inventing visible wording [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/create/changelog.md:61]. Neither Compact nor Expanded, no ceiling and no exemplar appears in its 70 lines. Consequence for Q5: the command doc is not an edit target for format, only a routing hop.
sources: `.skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/references/README.md:47` (names the presentation file as the command-surface asset)

keyFindings.text: **The command surface duplicates the two-tier threshold instead of deferring, then defers for the rest — three copies in the autonomous path, two in the interactive path.** Auto defines COMPACT at "fewer than 10 changes and no breaking change" and EXPANDED at "10+ changes, a major bump, or any breaking change" in the template comment block [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/create/assets/create-changelog-auto.yaml:287], restates the thresholds in a FORMAT SELECTION comment immediately below [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/create/assets/create-changelog-auto.yaml:293], and encodes them a third time as executable step logic [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/create/assets/create-changelog-auto.yaml:539], while also pointing away for detail: "See template file Section 5 (Format Selection Guide) for full rules" [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/create/assets/create-changelog-auto.yaml:541]. Confirm keeps the comment definition [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/create/assets/create-changelog-confirm.yaml:283] and the executable copy [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/create/assets/create-changelog-confirm.yaml:533] but drops both the FORMAT SELECTION comment and the Section-5 pointer. So the answer to sub-part 1 is *both*: duplicated at the tier level, deferred at the rule level, and the copy that actually decides is the executable one, not the template.
sources: `.skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/references/README.md:47` (names the presentation file as the command-surface asset)

keyFindings.text: **The completion display scores the quantities the long format maximises.** The result template reports "Sections: [section_count]" and "Files Tracked: [files_changed_count]" [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/create/assets/create-changelog-presentation.txt:155], and both YAML completion reports repeat the section count [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/create/assets/create-changelog-auto.yaml:812]. "Files Tracked" surfaces a file-count metric that the body rules simultaneously forbid in prose — no Files Changed tables [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/create/assets/create-changelog-auto.yaml:577]. The run is therefore scored on volume while the writer is told to hide volume, and nothing in the report measures the reader-facing property the short entry is built for.
sources: `.skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/references/README.md:47` (names the presentation file as the command-surface asset)

keyFindings.text: **The release step imposes no body constraint, so whatever length the workflow produced is what publishes.** Release-notes preparation strips the YAML frontmatter block and the editorial H1, keeps the entry's spacing, appends an ` ` rule plus a "Full changelog:" footer and writes the result to a notes file [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/create/assets/create-changelog-auto.yaml:717], [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/create/assets/create-changelog-confirm.yaml:654], which is then handed straight to `gh release create` [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/create/assets/create-changelog-auto.yaml:728]. The only body rules in that step are presentational: no duplicated title H1 [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/create/assets/create-changelog-confirm.yaml:658] and the spacing convention [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/create/assets/create-changelog-confirm.yaml:659]. The answer to sub-part 4 is that the release step does not constrain the body at all — it inherits it, so an over-long entry becomes a public release note verbatim, and the last gate before publication is step 5's per-unit checks from finding 4.
sources: `.skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/references/README.md:47` (names the presentation file as the command-surface asset)

keyFindings.text: **Upgrade-note guidance is action-typed but never section-ordered, and the two files disagree in depth.** The autonomous path specifies Adopt/Repoint/Drop lead-ins, a "No migration required." fallback, one action per line with no rationale, and the `## Upgrade` versus `## Upgrade Notes` name split [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/create/assets/create-changelog-auto.yaml:597]. The interactive path compresses all of that into a single clause [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/create/assets/create-changelog-confirm.yaml:551]. "in section order" occurs exactly once in each file and only for glance bullets in the extend branch — "Add one glance bullet per new theme, in section order" [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/create/assets/create-changelog-auto.yaml:608], [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/create/assets/create-changelog-confirm.yaml:559] — and the adjacent upgrade clause says only "any action to Upgrade Notes" with no ordering [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/create/assets/create-changelog-auto.yaml:609]. Sub-part 5 therefore answers "action-typed, not section-ordered": the ordering rule iteration 1 observed in the short entry has no carrier on the command surface.
sources: `.skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-changelog/references/README.md:47` (names the presentation file as the command-surface asset)

keyFindings.text: **"Upgrade notes ordered by section": the premise needs an attribution rule the format does not state — this is a contradiction in the brief, recorded rather than halted (no operator present).** Under a literal reading the short entry's upgrade list is not monotonic: `Callers of sk-design-fundamentals` maps to `Retired Surfaces` (section 6) and the next-but-one note maps to `Frontend Surface` (section 2). [SOURCE: .skilled/changelog/skilled/v4.0.1.0.md:179-195] The list becomes monotonic under a different rule — *a retirement's note is attributed to the section that names its replacement* — leaving exactly one note with no section at all, the advisor rebuild [SOURCE: .skilled/changelog/skilled/v4.0.1.0.md:183]. So the truthful statement of the rule is "ordered by section, with a retirement attributed to its replacement", and it is only mechanically checkable once the entry declares a section list and notes carry a section reference. Recording as a Q5 constraint: do not ship an order check before the template carries the mapping.

**`h2DividerRequired: true` is inert for changelogs.** The check collects H2s matching `^##\s+(\d+)\.\s+(.+?)\s*$` whose title is caps-only. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/shared/scripts/validate_document.py:677-682] A changelog H2 is unnumbered title case (`## What's New at a Glance` [SOURCE: .skilled/changelog/skilled/v4.0.1.0.md:39]), so the rule declared for this type [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/shared/assets/template-rules.json:487] can never fire on a conforming entry.

**`hvr_scan.py` is not part of the changelog pipeline at all.** It is a prose scanner for the human-voice standard: it parses `hvr-rules.md` at run time rather than carrying term lists [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-with-human-voice/scripts/hvr_scan.py:55-58], and its own docstring limits it to "punctuation bans, the hard blocker words of section 6, the phrase blockers of section 7, and the soft deductions of section 8", explicitly excluding structural and voice findings that need a reader. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-with-human-voice/scripts/hvr_scan.py:15-21] A grep for `hvr_scan` across `.skilled/skills/sk-doc` and `.skilled/commands` finds only that packet's own changelog entries, references and playbook pages — no invocation from the changelog skill, the command YAMLs or `validate_document.py`. It has no changelog mode, no section model and no length model, so Q4's answer for `hvr_scan.py` is: nothing to extend, and adding one would duplicate a validator whose whole design is type-agnostic prose.

**At-a-glance bullet order: not mechanically checkable today, and no validator edit can make it so.** The bullets' bold leads are prose, not section names — `**Each skill keeps its router in its own file.**` sits under `## Skill Routing`, `**More requests reach the right skill.**` under the same section. [SOURCE: .skilled/changelog/skilled/v4.0.1.0.md:41-48] Mapping bullet to section needs semantics. This is a template dependency for Q5: order becomes checkable only if the template makes each bullet declare its section (a bold section-name prefix or a trailing section tag), after which a monotonic-index check over the emitted section order is trivial. Recording it as a constraint, not a defect.

**At-a-glance presence and size: mechanical.** A count-ratio test discriminates where presence alone does not, because the long version has the section too (`## What's New at a Glance` at long line 50). Short: 8 bullets against 22 H4s (8 ≥ ⌈22/4⌉ = 6, passes). Long: 8 bullets against 38 H4s (8 < ⌈38/4⌉ = 10, fails). The short entry's section is at line 39 with 8 bullets. [SOURCE: .skilled/changelog/skilled/v4.0.1.0.md:39-48] Implementation: a new `validate_changelog_shape(content, file_path)` beside `validate_changelog_omissions` and called from the `doc_type == 'changelog'` branch [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/shared/scripts/validate_document.py:3049-3051]; the H2 normalisation already exists as `normalize_section_name`. Severity should start at `warning`, because a small release legitimately has no at-a-glance list.

**Content checking is exactly two regexes, both `warning` severity.** `CHANGELOG_INTERNAL_ID` matches `[A-Z]{2,4}-\d{3}` or `T\d{3}` minus the algorithm-name prefixes (`SHA`, `AES`, `RSA`, `CRC`, `DES`); `CHANGELOG_TEST_COUNT` matches `\b\d+\s+(?:cases|tests|PASS lines)\b`. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/shared/scripts/validate_document.py:2675-2684] The frontmatter block and every `>` line are exempt, and inline code spans are masked before the match. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/shared/scripts/validate_document.py:2701-2709] Two warnings is the entire body-level contract enforcement in the repository today.

**Document type is decided by folder, before the filename.** A path containing `/changelog/` returns `('changelog', 'rule')`, and only then does the type-specific code run. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/shared/scripts/validate_document.py:305-310]

**Every render check is skipped for entries.** `validate_render_checks` returns `[]` when `renderChecks` is absent and `sectionReferenceChecks` is false [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/shared/scripts/validate_document.py:1686-1689], which is the changelog configuration [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/shared/assets/template-rules.json:501]. So the bold-label-join, setext, bare-url, repeated-label, H2-sequence and section-citation checks never run on an entry. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/shared/scripts/validate_document.py:1693-1705]

**File-total ceiling: no infrastructure, and it cannot be blocking without retrofitting the exemplar.** A 240-line body ceiling passes short (197) and fails long (339), but the canonical exemplar is 535 lines [SOURCE: .skilled/changelog/skilled/v4.0.0.0.md], so a blocking total ceiling fails `validate.sh --strict` on the tree the moment it lands. Ship it as `warning` first, or gate it to entries at or below a version cut. This is the sharpest dependency in Q5: the exemplar and the ceiling cannot both be canonical.

**Five frontmatter checks, all blocking**: block missing, block unclosed, any required key missing, `trigger_phrases` declared but empty, and a version file with no phrase naming its version. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/shared/scripts/validate_document.py:2604-2677] The required-key list is read from the rules file, not hardcoded: `title, description, trigger_phrases, importance_tier, contextType`. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/shared/assets/template-rules.json:492-499]

**Folded small fixes: heuristic, and good enough at `warning`.** Detector: inside one H2, if there are ≥ 5 H4s and ≥ 3 of them have a bullet-less body under 30 words, emit `changelog_unfolded_fixes`. Test: the short `## Runtimes and Fixes` has 2 H4s, one prose and one 4-item list under `#### Smaller Fixes` [SOURCE: .skilled/changelog/skilled/v4.0.1.0.md:146-158], so it does not trigger; the long version's same section splits the same fixes into 7 separate H4s [INFERENCE: `git show bc28fcbbba:...` section `## Runtimes and Fixes`, headings at lines 258-278], so it does. This check also needs the template to supply a canonical fold heading, which Q2/Q5 own.

**H4 item-count ceiling: mechanical.** Total ≤ 26 passes short (22) and fails long (38); per-section ≤ 5 passes short (max 5) and fails long (max 7 with three sections at 5+). Both belong in the new `validate_changelog_shape` with module-level constants next to `CHANGELOG_ENTRY_NAME` [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/shared/scripts/validate_document.py:2558] and can reuse `_fenced_line_numbers` for masking.

**H4 narrative length: mechanical.** Cap the words in an H4 body at 90: short's longest is 80, long's is 148. Fenced code and bullet lists must be excluded from the count (the short entry's longest H4 body by bullet count is a 16-item list [SOURCE: .skilled/changelog/skilled/v4.0.1.0.md:173-178]), and severity must be `warning` — one long paragraph can be legitimate in a legal entry.

**Maintainer-only detail beyond test counts: not separable by vocabulary, and the kept entry proves it.** The short entry names `package_skill.py --strict` [SOURCE: .skilled/changelog/skilled/v4.0.1.0.md:60], `skill-advisor.cjs` [SOURCE: .skilled/changelog/skilled/v4.0.1.0.md:183], a token delta (`328,333` to `238,406`) [SOURCE: .skilled/changelog/skilled/v4.0.1.0.md:56] and a spelled-out count of render checks [SOURCE: .skilled/changelog/skilled/v4.0.1.0.md:171]. Every one of those is on the keep side of the target format, so any lexical "internal tooling" or "number in prose" ban deletes material the exemplar retains. Consequence for Q5: the drop rule stays prose in the template and skill, and the validator may enforce only shapes it can name — internal ids, test accounting, `(Level N)`. Code spans already mask the tool names [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/shared/scripts/validate_document.py:2679-2681], which is why they survive the current checks.

**No length rule exists anywhere.** Greps for `maxLines|max_length|ceiling|maxWords` over `validate_document.py` and `template-rules.json` return zero hits, and the changelog block declares no length key between its section lists and its frontmatter contract. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/shared/assets/template-rules.json:451-502] This extends iteration 3's finding (no ceiling in the command YAMLs) to the validator side: nothing in the pipeline measures an entry's size.

**Only entry-shaped files get the changelog checks.** `CHANGELOG_ENTRY_NAME` matches `v\d+(\.\d+){1,3}.md` or `changelog-*.md`; a `README.md` in the same folder keeps only the generic structural rules. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/shared/scripts/validate_document.py:2554-2558] Both changelog validators early-return on this gate [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/shared/scripts/validate_document.py:2617-2618] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/shared/scripts/validate_document.py:2697-2698]

**Section rules are inert twice over.** `requiredSections` is empty, so nothing can be required [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/shared/assets/template-rules.json:453]; and the finder that would check it only scans `^## \d+\.\s+[^\n]+` [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/shared/scripts/validate_document.py:1834], which an unnumbered changelog H2 cannot match. Populating `requiredSections` alone would change nothing.

**Spec-folder `(Level N)`: mechanical and cheap, but blocked by a deliberate exemption.** The only reason it is missing today is that every `>` line is skipped wholesale [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/shared/scripts/validate_document.py:2707-2709], because that line is where packet labels are allowed to live. The narrow fix is a third regex applied *to* the blockquote instead of masking it: flag `\((?:Level|L)\s*\d\)` on a line starting `> Spec folder`. Short has none [SOURCE: .skilled/changelog/skilled/v4.0.1.0.md:27]; long has one.
**The two entries separate cleanly on four mechanical measures, and not at all on the fifth.**

ruledOutDirections.text: **A pure word-level diff as the source of the rules.** The rewording between the two versions is small; nearly all of the 144-line difference is deleted or merged H4 blocks.
